newsitem.title: USA: U.S. concerned by Ecuador's political crisis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. concerned by Ecuador's political crisis.

text.p: The United States voiced concern Friday over the constitutional crisis crippling Ecuador, where three senior politicians are claiming to be the president.

The State Department, noting that all three claimants had called for public demonstrations of support, advised against travel to parts of the capital, Quito, saying the situation had "the potential for becoming violent."
"There continue to be localised demonstrations ...and there have been sporadic incidents of violence. Travelers should use discretion," a written statement said.

Americans were encouraged to seek updated information on security in Ecuador from the U.S. Embassy in Quito and advised not to travel to the colonial part of the capital, particularly the area around the presidential palace.
At least one person was killed in disturbances outside the palace Friday as ousted President Abdala Bucaram defied calls for his removal.
Riot police, backed by armoured personnel carriers and water cannon, fired tear gas into the crowd of protesters who fought back with rocks and homemade gasoline bombs.
The White House, however, noted with some relief that the Ecuadorean armed forces had not taken sides in the political tug-of-war.
"We are reminding everyone that the rule of law applies, that it is important for constitutional processes to be followed," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.

"But we are encouraged by the statements being made by the military leadership of Ecuador, indicating that they...don't intend to play any role in the resolution of the current disagreements about the presidency," he added.
The constitutional crisis started late Thursday when the Congress ousted Bucaram and replaced him with Speaker Fabian Alarcon.
Bucaram, a flamboyant populist, defiantly refused to go, but his vicepresident, Rosalia Arteaga, quickly issued a decree appointing herself as president.
Since then the country's defence minister, a general loyal to Bucaram, has declared a nationwide state of emergency to quell protest against his president.
Earlier Friday, the State Department urged the political leadership in Quito to resolve its disputes peacefully and within the bounds of law.
